subject: Linguistics
title: The Cocktail Party Effect
description: A quick, practical guide to The Cocktail Party Effect.

hook.text: At a noisy party, someone says your name across the room—and your attention snaps to it instantly.

buildup.text: The cocktail party effect is the ability to focus on one voice while filtering out background noise.

discovery.text: Cherry studied this in 1953—showing that we use pitch, location, and familiarity to filter voices.

twist.text: Your brain monitors unattended speech at a low level—emotionally significant words break through.

climax.text: This selective attention relies on both bottom-up acoustic cues and top-down expectations.

punchline.text: Your brain listens to everything—but only lets some things through.

quiz.question: What breaks through the attention filter in the cocktail party effect?
options: Emotionally significant words like your name
